context.question: At fixed total heating energy, can the system find a heating profile that improves integrated simulated fusion energy, and does that improvement survive stricter checks?

verification_budget.note: Verification runs only after the search finalist is frozen.

hypotheses.title: Measure the frozen ITER-hybrid heating baseline
hypotheses.prediction: E_fusion is finite and heating energy is 51 MJ at 1.0 s.
hypotheses.assessment: Baseline E_fusion=110.36053618063139 MJ at 51 MJ heating. Reference only; not an improvement claim.

decision.hypothesis: At fixed 51 MJ, more on-axis deposition than the measured baseline raises core-weighted fusion yield.
decision.prediction: E_fusion exceeds the measured 110.36053618063139 MJ at location=0.05, width=0.07280908366127758.
decision.rationale: The only completed run is the ITER-hybrid baseline: location=0.12741589640723575, width=0.07280908366127758, E_fusion=110.36053618063139 MJ, peak Ti=16.655230458088397 keV, all checks passed. Transport is constant-χ, so heat stays near the deposit; fusion is core-weighted. The first contrast therefore holds width fixed at the measured baseline value and moves location to the on-axis bound 0.05, isolating whether more central heating increases integrated P_fusion.
